topic: Strands Agents SDK Tutorial: Build AWS-Native AI Agents in Minutes

key_points: Quickstart presents two patterns: Graph API and Functional API for building calculator-style agents.
Requires an Anthropic model key for the sample flow and supports multi-step graph-based orchestration.
Emphasizes runtime concepts and tooling for building production workflows from graph primitives.
Creates a CrewAI Flow project via CLI and scaffolds a stateful `Flow` with `crews/content_crew`.
Researcher use case writes a report artifact to `output/report.md` as a concrete end-to-end path.
Supports web-search tools like Serper and LLM provider configuration in a role/task-based model.
Build agents with a simple `Agent` and `Runner`, then add tool decorators via `@function_tool`.
Supports multi-agent routing through `handoffs`, with the runner orchestrating tool calls and handoff selection.
Includes trace visibility through OpenAI Dashboard and a dedicated sandbox mode for file/workspace tasks.
Introduces `FunctionAgent` and async run loop pattern that returns tool calls and re-enters the agent with updated context.
Supports multiple prompting strategies beyond FunctionAgent, including ReAct and CodeAct style agents.
Explicitly highlights memory and tool specification patterns as core building blocks for reliability.
Targets quick startup with AgentCore CLI (`agentcore create/deploy/invoke`) and AWS SDK paths.
Highlights AWS prerequisite constraints (preview regions and CLI/boto3 versions), making readiness planning important.
Emphasizes session continuity (`runtimeSessionId`) and harness lifecycle management for repeated invocations.

stats.fact: AWS Compute Blog says Gartner forecasts that by 2028 over 33% of enterprise applications will embed agentic capabilities, up from <1%.
Strands Agents SDK documentation highlights a quick start goal of setting up a first agent in under 20 minutes.
GitHub repo star counts in early June 2026: Strands SDK Python ~6106, CrewAI ~53279, LangGraph ~34458, LlamaIndex ~50082, OpenAI Agents Python ~27084.
An arXiv paper (May 2026) reports agent orchestration frameworks collectively exceeding 290,000 GitHub stars across major open-source ecosystems.
AWS Bedrock AgentCore was described as in preview at the time of publication of the AWS serverless guide and is presented as a way to standardize memory, sessions, and production-grade observability.

angles: Position Strands as the fastest migration path for teams already standardizing on Python on AWS Lambda/ECS, because it is already model-agnostic and AWS-native in deployment posture.
Contrast Strands vs. OpenAI/CrewAI/LangGraph by control-plane philosophy: model-driven loops and simplicity vs. graph-heavy or platform-specific orchestration.
Use AWS Bedrock AgentCore in place of custom orchestration when governance, identity, and OTEL observability requirements dominate over framework flexibility.
Add a production-hardening section (state, session management, auth, observability) to differentiate from pure beginner tutorials and increase enterprise relevance.
Use `MCP` tooling emphasis as a bridge point, since multiple frameworks now expose MCP-compatible integrations for tool access.
outline: H2: Why this tutorial is AWS-native (Strands vs alternatives)
H2: Prerequisites and repository setup for a 20-minute working prototype
H2: Build your first Strands agent (Python/TypeScript) and connect tools
H2: Session state, memory, and tool orchestration for production behavior
H2: Deploy to AWS (Lambda/AgentCore) with observability, identity, and security checks
H2: Framework comparison and when to switch
